notes.testing: TSR (kingdoms/tsr, typed_depth Some(2)) on feynman_I_26_2, Snell's law theta1 = arcsin(n*sin(theta2)). THIS IS THE DEPTH-2 CASE THE T2 RUNG EXISTS FOR: a transcendental applied to something containing another transcendental. A ceiling at T1 would have made this law unreachable, so it is the direct test of the spec's central choice of two rather than one.
notes.outcome: LAW RECOVERED IN ITS TRUE FORM at generation 169 in 18.1 s, by early_stop: asin((x_0*sin(x_1))). Columns are n, theta2, so this is arcsin(n*sin(theta2)) symbol for symbol against pmlb metadata.yaml. train 1-R2 1.598e-14, validation 1.716e-14, log10 p -35.68, test R2 1.000000. 107.3 ms/generation. 32,262 genes refused on type = 5.30% of gene-slots per generation; 0 oversized. Final depth histogram 0:185 1:2352 2:810 3:173 4:47 5:23 6:6 7:4 -- 810 genes sit AT the T2 ceiling, and the recovered law is itself depth 2, so the ceiling was reached, used, and correct. THE SPEC'S CHOICE OF TWO IS VINDICATED BY DIRECT MEASUREMENT: at a ceiling of one this law has no legal signature and could not have been found.

notes.testing: MATCHED CHECK added after the sweep, for the same reason.
notes.outcome: THE EARLIER NOTE ON THIS CARD OVERCLAIMED. Untyped at seed 7014, same budget, ALSO recovers this law -- at generation 201 against TSR's 169, reporting -asin(-(x_0*sin(x_1))). And at seed 7015 both typed and untyped find it at generation 2, because the counter-based generator draws identical initial tokens for any slot within budget. So I.26.2 is NOT evidence for typing. What it does establish is that the T2 rung is NECESSARY: at a ceiling of T1 this law has no legal signature and the engine would have lost a law it can otherwise find.
